chapters.title: 费城飞人队赢得世界大赛？——冠词引入
chapters.summary: 詹姆斯以费城飞人队赢得世界大赛这一（虚构的）棒球事件开场，并指出自己在讲述中频繁使用了“the”和“a”，由此引出对冠词的讨论。
chapters.english_summary: James opens by claiming the Philadelphia Flyers won the World Series, then notes that he used the words 'the' and 'a' a lot, setting up a lesson on articles.

points.title: 詹姆斯开场并提及费城飞人队赢得世界大赛
指出讲述中频繁使用“the”和“a”

chapters.title: 冠词入门：冠词的作用与重要性
chapters.summary: 本单元引入冠词这一主题，指出许多外语学习者在掌握词汇和语法后常忽略冠词。讲解冠词能表明名词是单数还是复数，并提示看到冠词通常意味着单数，但冠词的作用不止于此，为后续深入讲解做铺垫。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces the topic of articles, noting that many foreign students master vocabulary and grammar but overlook articles. It explains that articles indicate whether something is singular or plural, and that seeing an article generally means singular, while hinting that articles do more than that.

points.title: 引入冠词主题
学习者常忽略冠词
冠词表明单复数
冠词作用不止于此

chapters.title: 冠词记忆法：a 与 the 用于单数名词
chapters.summary: 本段介绍一个记忆冠词的简单方法：单词 article 中的 a 对应冠词 a，t 对应冠词 the。讲解指出 a 和 the 都用于单数对象，并用 a pen 和 the pen is blue 作为例句，说明同一支笔可以先用 a 再用 the 指代。
chapters.english_summary: This unit presents a mnemonic for articles: the letters a and t in the word article stand for a and the. It explains that a and the are used for singular objects, using a pen and the pen is blue as examples, and notes that the same pen can be referred to first with a and then with the.

points.title: 用 article 一词记忆 a 和 the
a 和 the 用于单数对象
例句：a pen 与 the pen is blue
同一支笔先用 a 再用 the

chapters.title: 冠词a与the的用法区别及记忆技巧
chapters.summary: 本单元讲解英语冠词a和the的基本区别：a用于泛指或首次提及的事物，the用于特指或双方已知的事物。通过“This is a pen”和“The pen's over there”等例子，说明当说话双方不清楚所指对象时用a，当指向具体对象时用the，并提供一个帮助记忆的小技巧。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the difference between the articles 'a' and 'the': 'a' is used for general things or first mentions, while 'the' is used for specific things. It uses examples like 'This is a pen' and 'The pen's over there' to show that 'a' is used when the listener doesn't know which thing is meant, and 'the' when pointing to a specific object. A memory trick is also introduced.

points.title: a用于泛指，the用于特指
首次提及且为泛指时用a
说话双方不清楚所指时用a
指向具体对象时用the

chapters.title: 冠词a与the的用法区别：泛指与双方已知
chapters.summary: 本单元讲解冠词a和the的两个使用条件。a用于泛指一般事物，且听话人不知道所指对象；the不仅用于特定事物，还用于双方或所有人都知道所指对象的情况。通过Ezekiel举办派对、Josh是否知情的对话例子说明：Josh不知情时说a party，Josh已知情时说the party。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains two cases for using articles. It states that 'a' is used for general things and when not everyone knows what you are talking about, while 'the' is used not only for specific things but also when both people or all people know what you are talking about. It illustrates this with an example about a party hosted by Ezekiel and whether Josh knows about it, contrasting 'I'm going to a party' with 'I'm going to the party.'

points.title: a的两个使用条件：泛指且对方不知情
Ezekiel派对例子：Josh不知情时说a party
Josh已知情时说the party
the用于双方或所有人都知道所指对象

chapters.title: 冠词用法复习：a 与 the 的区别
chapters.summary: 本段复习冠词 a 和 the 的用法区别。a 用于泛指事物，或当并非所有人都知道所谈论的内容时；the 用于特指事物，或当所有人都知道所谈论的内容时。讲者提到之后会在蓝屏上显示小测试，让学习者回忆哪个定义对应哪个冠词。
chapters.english_summary: This unit reviews the distinction between the articles 'a' and 'the'. 'A' is used for general things or when not everyone knows what is being discussed; 'the' is used for specific things or when all people know what is being talked about. The speaker mentions a follow-up test on the blue screen to match definitions with the correct article.

points.title: 提到蓝屏小测试以巩固记忆
a 用于泛指或信息不为所有人所知
the 用于特指或信息为所有人所知

chapters.title: 冠词 a 与 an 的用法区别
chapters.summary: 本段讲解冠词 a 和 an 的使用规则：一般情况下用 a，但当后面单词以元音开头时，a 要变为 an，例如 an elephant、an apple；而像 university、European 这类以“you”音开头的单词，仍用 a。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the difference between the articles 'a' and 'an': 'a' changes to 'an' before vowel sounds, as in 'an elephant' and 'an apple', but words beginning with a 'you' sound, such as 'university' or 'European', still take 'a'.

points.title: a 变为 an 的规则
元音开头的例子：an elephant, an apple
以“you”音开头的单词仍用 a：a university, European

chapters.title: 课程总结与冠词用法回顾
chapters.summary: 本单元是课程结尾，讲师总结已解决的问题，预告后续介词课程，并回顾冠词用法：泛指用a/an（an用于元音前），特指或众所周知的事物用the，最后以轻松方式结束课程。
chapters.english_summary: This unit is the closing of the lesson. The instructor summarizes the problem just addressed, mentions that another issue will come up later and that prepositions will be a separate lesson, then reviews article usage: use 'a' or 'an' for one general thing (with 'an' before vowels) and 'the' for specific things or things everyone knows about. The lesson ends with a light-hearted check and a farewell.

points.title: 预告后续课程：介词
回顾冠词用法：泛指用a/an，特指用the
轻松结束课程

chapters.title: 课程结束与 engVid 网站推荐
chapters.summary: 讲师在结束前向学习者推荐 engVid 网站，说明可以在该网站找到包括自己在内的多位老师，帮助解决冠词、介词及其他语法点、发音和听力等问题，并邀请大家访问论坛。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker gives a closing message recommending engVid, saying learners can find teachers including the speaker to help with articles, prepositions, other grammar points, pronunciation, and listening, and invites viewers to the forum before saying goodbye.

points.title: 推荐 engVid 网站
网站可提供的帮助范围
邀请访问论坛并道别

videos.title: How Model Context Protocol (MCP) actually works
videos.creator: Google Cloud Tech

chapters.title: 模型上下文协议（MCP）简介与视频概览
chapters.summary: 视频开头指出让AI模型与工具或数据交互时存在混乱：每个API行为不同、每次集成需要定制代码、模型变化会破坏连接。为此引入了模型上下文协议（MCP）。视频将介绍MCP是什么、为何存在、如何改变模型与世界交互的方式，并逐步讲解核心概念、与传统API的对比，以及对开发者和AI应用的意义。
chapters.english_summary: The video opens by noting that connecting AI models to tools or data is messy: every API behaves differently, each integration needs custom code, and model changes break connections. It introduces the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the fix. The video promises to explain what MCP is, why it exists, and how it changes how models interact with the world, covering core ideas step by step, comparisons to traditional APIs, and implications for developers building agents or AI-powered applications.

points.title: AI模型与工具/数据交互的痛点
MCP的引入及其目的
视频内容概览：核心概念、API对比与开发者意义

chapters.title: 什么是模型上下文协议（MCP）
chapters.summary: 介绍模型上下文协议（MCP）的核心定义：它是由 Anthropic 推出的开放标准，用于以一致且结构化的方式将模型连接到工具、数据和上下文，相当于模型与其周边系统之间的共享语言。它定义了模型如何发现可用工具、请求信息并执行操作，而无需了解每个工具的具体实现细节，从而解决当前 AI 开发中如何让模型安全可靠地使用外部资源这一痛点。
chapters.english_summary: Defines the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as an open standard introduced by Anthropic for connecting models to tools, data, and context in a consistent, structured way. It acts as a shared language between models and surrounding systems, defining how a model can discover available tools, request information, and perform actions without knowing each tool's implementation details, addressing the pain point of making models use external resources safely and reliably.

points.title: MCP 是连接模型与工具、数据、上下文的开放标准
MCP 如同模型与周边系统之间的共享语言
MCP 定义模型如何发现工具、请求信息并执行操作
由 Anthropic 推出并正在被行业采用
解决如何让模型安全可靠地使用外部资源的问题

chapters.title: MCP 为何重要：弥合 API 与语言模型之间的鸿沟
chapters.summary: 本段解释传统 API 是为能提出精确、确定性请求的程序设计的，而语言模型以概率方式生成文本、处理不确定输入，常需先提问或探索。MCP 通过提供结构化方式让模型发现和描述可用资源（函数、数据集、文档、提示），以一致接口替代硬编码集成，使模型能动态查询、使用并串联多个工具，同时处于安全标准化框架内。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains why MCP matters: traditional APIs were designed for programs that form precise, deterministic requests, whereas language models generate text probabilistically, reason about uncertain inputs, and often need to ask questions or explore first. MCP bridges this gap by giving models a structured way to discover and describe available resources such as functions, data sets, documents, or prompts through a consistent interface, letting them dynamically query and use what is available and chain multiple tools together within a safe, standardized framework instead of hard coding every integration.

points.title: 传统 API 面向确定性程序请求
语言模型以概率方式生成并处理不确定输入
MCP 提供结构化资源发现与描述
一致接口替代硬编码集成
动态查询、使用并串联工具，保持安全标准化

chapters.title: MCP 工作原理：客户端与服务器
chapters.summary: 解释 MCP 的核心架构：协议分为客户端和服务器两侧。客户端通常是语言模型或代理系统，服务器是暴露资源的环境。服务器连接后会声明其支持的能力、资源和操作，使模型无需预先编程即可动态发现 API。双方通过简单明确定义的 schema 通信，客户端发送请求，服务器返回结构化 JSON。
chapters.english_summary: Explains the core architecture of MCP: the protocol has two sides, clients and servers. The client is usually the language model or agent system, while the server is the environment exposing resources. Upon connection, the server advertises its supported capabilities, resources, and actions, allowing the model to dynamically discover APIs without pre-programming. Communication uses a simple, well-defined schema where the client sends requests and the server responds with structured JSON.

points.title: 协议分为客户端和服务器两侧
客户端通常是语言模型或代理系统
服务器是暴露资源的环境
服务器声明支持的能力和资源，模型可动态发现
通信通过简单明确定义的 schema，返回结构化 JSON

chapters.title: MCP 协议的核心资源类型：工具、资源、提示与上下文
chapters.summary: 本段深入讲解 MCP 协议定义的几类主要资源类型：工具是模型可调用的动作（如搜索数据库、发邮件、分析文件）；资源是数据与状态（如文本文档、数据库记录、图像）；提示是描述模型在特定任务中行为的可复用模板；上下文是模型可引入推理过程的外部信息（如聊天历史、公司数据、用户偏好）。MCP 客户端连接后可向服务器请求这些内容的列表，每个工具或资源都带有描述其功能、输入与输出的元数据，使模型能智能交互。协议在所有工具间强制统一 schema，因此无论使用 GitHub、CRM 还是日历服务器，模型都使用同一种语言。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the main MCP resource types: tools as invokable actions (e.g., search database, send email, analyze a file), resources as data and state (e.g., text document, database record, image), prompts as reusable templates for model behavior on specific tasks, and context as external information pulled into reasoning (e.g., chat history, company data, user preferences). It also covers how an MCP client can request lists of these from the server, how each tool or resource carries metadata about its function, expected input, and returned output, and how the protocol enforces a consistent schema so models speak the same language across GitHub, CRM, or calendar servers.

points.title: 工具是模型可调用的动作，例如搜索数据库、发送邮件或分析文件
资源是数据与状态，例如文本文档、数据库记录或图像
提示是描述模型在特定任务中行为的可复用模板
上下文是模型可引入推理过程的外部信息，如聊天历史、公司数据或用户偏好
客户端可请求资源列表，元数据与统一 schema 让模型跨服务器智能交互

chapters.title: 为什么需要 MCP：面向模型的 API 抽象层
chapters.summary: 本单元解释已有 API 的情况下为何还需要 MCP，核心在于消费者不同：API 面向人类编写的程序，MCP 面向像人类一样推理的模型。MCP 可视为 API 之上的抽象层，API 依然存在，MCP 只是让它们对模型更友好。底层 MCP 服务器可能仍调用现有的 REST 或 GraphQL API，但模型只通过结构化的 MCP schema 交互，该 schema 统一处理发现、验证和执行，从而无需每次定制集成即可将系统暴露给任何兼容模型。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains why MCP is needed even when APIs already exist, focusing on the difference in consumers: APIs are designed for programs written by humans, while MCP is designed for models that reason like humans. MCP is described as an abstraction above APIs; APIs still exist, and MCP makes them model friendly. Under the hood, an MCP server might still call existing REST or GraphQL APIs, but the model only interacts through the structured MCP schema, which handles discovery, validation, and execution uniformly, allowing a system to be exposed to any compliant model without custom integrations each time.

points.title: 核心问题：已有 API 为何还需要 MCP
关键区别在于消费者：API 面向人类程序，MCP 面向推理模型
MCP 是 API 之上的抽象层，让 API 对模型友好
底层仍可调用 REST 或 GraphQL API，模型只通过 MCP schema 交互
MCP schema 统一处理发现、验证和执行，无需定制集成

chapters.title: MCP 实践示例：个人助理代理的集成对比
chapters.summary: 通过构建个人助理代理的示例，对比传统 API 集成方式与 MCP 方式。传统方式需为 Google Calendar、Notion、Gmail 分别编写代码、处理认证和边缘情况，并用冗长脆弱的系统提示教模型使用端点；MCP 方式则安装各系统服务器，服务器声明能力，模型自动发现工具并推理使用顺序和数据传递，开发者无需编写胶水代码，因为协议一致。
chapters.english_summary: A practical example compares building a personal assistant agent with traditional API integrations versus MCP. In the old approach, developers integrate Google Calendar, Notion, and Gmail APIs, write code for each service, handle authentication, rate limits, and edge cases, and teach the model via long fragile system prompts. With MCP, developers build or install servers for each system (calendar, note, email), each advertising capabilities; the model automatically sees available tools like list events, get meeting summary, or send email, and reasons about what to use, in what order, and what data to pass. The key difference is no glue code per new tool because the protocol is consistent.

points.title: 传统集成方式：为每个服务编写代码并处理认证与边缘情况
传统方式依赖冗长脆弱的系统提示教模型使用端点
MCP 方式：为各系统安装服务器，服务器声明能力
模型自动发现工具并推理使用顺序与数据传递
关键区别：开发者无需为每个新工具编写胶水代码，协议一致

chapters.title: MCP 统一模型与工具的通信方式
chapters.summary: 本段指出 MCP 正在像 HTTP 统一网络那样统一模型与工具的通信方式，因此现在学习它很重要，未来每个认真的 AI 开发者都需要让系统具备 MCP 意识。视频还引导观众查看描述栏中的 Google Cloud 相关 MCP 服务器列表和关于 MCP 服务器工作原理的博客文章，并推荐继续观看下一期视频《MCP versus API》。
chapters.english_summary: This closing segment states that MCP is beginning to unify how models talk to tools, similar to how HTTP unified the web, and argues that learning it now matters because AI developers will soon need to make their systems MCP aware. It points viewers to the description for a list of Google Cloud related MCP servers and a blog post about how MCP servers work, and recommends the next video titled MCP versus API.

points.title: MCP 正在统一模型与工具的通信
现在学习 MCP 的重要性
描述栏中的 Google Cloud MCP 服务器与博客资源
推荐下一期视频《MCP versus API》

videos.title: Why can’t governments print an unlimited amount of money? - Jonathan Smith
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 新冠疫情对经济的冲击与政府救助
chapters.summary: 2020年3月新冠疫情冲击全球经济，数百万人失业，许多企业倒闭，各国政府推出史上最大规模经济救助计划，美国首轮救助达2.2万亿美元。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces the March 2020 COVID-19 pandemic's impact on the global economy, including millions of job losses and business closures, and notes that governments responded with historically large economic relief packages, with the United States spending $2.2 trillion in a first round of relief.

points.title: 疫情冲击全球经济
大规模失业与企业倒闭
政府推出史上最大救助计划
美国首轮2.2万亿美元救助

chapters.title: 中央银行与货币供应量的管理
chapters.summary: 本段解释货币来源：多数国家由独立于政府的中央银行管理货币供应量，以防止政治干预。政府可通过减税和公共基建项目创造就业等经济政策，但不能直接增加货币供应量；货币流通量由中央银行决定。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains where money comes from: most countries have a central bank that manages the money supply and is independent from the government to prevent political interference. The government can implement economic policies such as decreasing taxes and creating jobs through public infrastructure projects, but it cannot directly increase the money supply; the central bank determines how much money is in circulation.

points.title: 中央银行管理货币供应量并独立于政府
政府可实施减税和公共基建等经济政策
政府不能直接增加货币供应量
中央银行决定货币流通量

chapters.title: 央行能否无限印钞救市
chapters.summary: 本段提出央行是否可以授权无限印钞来救助危机中的经济体这一问题，并指出这种做法虽可行，但只是短期方案，长期未必能促进经济增长，甚至可能损害经济。
chapters.english_summary: This unit raises the question of whether central banks can authorize printing unlimited money to help an economy in crisis, and states that while they could, it is only a short-term solution that may not boost long-term economic growth and can actually hurt the economy.

points.title: 提出央行无限印钞救市的问题
指出印钞只是短期方案
说明长期未必促进增长且可能损害经济

chapters.title: 货币流通增加为何导致通货膨胀
chapters.summary: 本段解释当流通中的货币增多时，食品、服装和汽车等商品制造商可以简单地通过涨价来应对需求，而不是增加生产、创造就业。结果是用同样多的钱买不到同样多的东西，这种情况称为通货膨胀。每年约2%的轻微通胀被视为经济健康的标志，但更高的通胀会迅速拖垮经济。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that when more money is in circulation, manufacturers of goods such as food, clothing, and cars could respond to demand by raising prices instead of producing more goods and creating jobs, meaning the same amount of money buys less—a situation called inflation. It notes that about 2% inflation per year is considered a sign of economic health, while more can quickly derail an economy.

points.title: 货币增多时制造商可涨价而非增产
同样金额购买力下降即通货膨胀
约2%年通胀被视为经济健康，更高则拖垮经济

chapters.title: 量化宽松与债券购买的基本原理
chapters.summary: 介绍近几十年来央行采用的量化宽松方法，即通过购买债券向经济注入现金，同时保持严重通胀的低风险。解释购买债券本质上是借钱给公司或政府，并说明个人购买债券使用已流通的货币，而央行购买债券则相当于创造新现金。
chapters.english_summary: Explains the quantitative easing approach used by central banks in recent decades to infuse the economy with cash while maintaining low risk of severe inflation. Describes how buying bonds is essentially loaning money to a company or government, and contrasts individual bond purchases using money already in circulation with central bank bond purchases that create new cash.

points.title: 量化宽松的目的：注入现金并控制通胀风险
央行通过购买债券增加现金流
购买债券的本质是借钱并收取利息
个人购买债券使用已流通货币
央行购买债券创造新现金

chapters.title: 美联储购买国债与2020年刺激计划
chapters.summary: 讲述2008-2009年金融危机和2020年期间，美国中央银行（美联储）从美国政府购买国债。国债历来被视为安全投资，因为政府会连本带息偿还。2020年初，美联储承诺无限量购买国债，向美国政府提供空前规模的贷款，这些现金被用于资助刺激支票和失业救济等救助措施。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that during the 2008-2009 financial crisis and again in 2020, the US central bank, the Federal Reserve, bought treasury bonds from the US government. Notes that historically many people bought these bonds as a safe investment because the government repays them with interest. In early 2020 the Federal Reserve pledged to buy unlimited treasury bonds, loaning the US government an unprecedented amount of money, cash the government used to fund relief efforts such as stimulus checks and unemployment benefits.

points.title: 美联储在2008-2009年危机和2020年购买国债
国债作为安全投资：政府连本带息偿还
2020年初美联储承诺无限量购买国债
资金用于刺激支票和失业救济等救助

chapters.title: 量化宽松并非印钞：通过购债压低收益率并激励放贷
chapters.summary: 本段说明美联储大量购买债券并不等同于印钞。由于债券定价方式，大规模购债会有效降低债券回报率，从而激励其他投资者向风险更高的实体（如中小公司）放贷以获取可观回报。这种鼓励放贷的方式应能帮助各类公司借款投入项目与招聘，长期提振经济，同时在短期内帮助政府向人们提供急需的现金。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that the Federal Reserve buying many bonds is not equivalent to printing money. Because of how bonds are priced, buying so many effectively lowers their return, which incentivizes other investors to lend to riskier entities such as small and midsize companies to get a decent return. Encouraging lending this way should help companies of all sizes borrow money for projects and hires, boosting the economy over time, while also helping the government supply people with urgently needed cash in the short term.

points.title: 购债不等同于印钞
大量购债压低债券回报率
低回报激励投资者向中小公司等风险更高实体放贷
鼓励放贷帮助各类公司借款投入项目与招聘
长期提振经济并短期帮助政府提供急需现金

chapters.title: 美联储无限购债引发的理论争议
chapters.summary: 本段讨论美联储承诺无限购买政府债务所引发的疑问。理论上，政府可发行更多债券由央行购买，再用新债所得偿还旧债，从而实际上无需向央行偿还债务。一些经济学家据此担忧央行购买政府债务颠覆了保护经济的体系，另一些人则认为这些措施必要且迄今有助于稳定经济。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that the Federal Reserve's pledge to buy unlimited government debt has raised questions. In theory, the government could issue more bonds for the central bank to purchase, then use the money from new bonds to pay off old bonds, effectively never repaying its debt to the central bank. Some economists cite this and other theoretical scenarios to argue that a central bank buying government debt subverts a system designed to protect the economy, while others insist these measures are necessary and have so far helped stabilize economies.

points.title: 美联储无限购债承诺引发疑问
理论循环：发新债还旧债，政府实际无需偿还央行债务
经济学家担忧：央行购债颠覆保护经济的体系
另一方观点：措施必要且迄今有助于稳定经济

chapters.title: 量化宽松仍属较新政策，潜在后果尚待显现
chapters.summary: 指出量化宽松近年来虽已更为常见，但仍属相对较新的政策工具，其潜在后果仍在逐步显现。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that although quantitative easing has become more common in recent years, it is still relatively new and its potential consequences are still unfolding.

points.title: 量化宽松近年更为常见
该政策仍相对较新，潜在后果尚在显现

videos.creator: Hung-yi Lee

chapters.title: 线性模型的局限：无法拟合复杂关系
chapters.summary: 说明线性模型过于简单：x1 与 y 的关系被限制为一条直线，调整 w 只改变斜率、调整 b 只改变与 y 轴交点，但无论怎么改都还是一条直线。以观看人数为例，指出真实关系可能先成正比、超过某峰值后反而下降，形成红色曲线般的关系，而线性模型永远无法产生这条线。
chapters.english_summary: Explains why a linear model is too simple: the relationship between x1 and y is constrained to a straight line, where changing w alters the slope and changing b shifts the y-axis intercept, yet the result always remains a straight line. Using a view-count example, it notes the real relationship might first be proportional and then decline after a peak, like a red curve, which a linear model can never produce.

points.title: 线性模型把 x1 与 y 的关系限定为直线
调整 w 改变斜率、调整 b 改变与 y 轴交点
观看人数例子：可能先成正比、过峰值后下降
线性模型无法制造红色曲线关系

chapters.title: 线性模型的限制与模型偏置（Model Bias）
chapters.summary: 本段指出线性模型存在很大限制，这种来自模型本身的限制称为 Model Bias，并强调它与公式中的参数 b（也叫 Bias）含义不同，容易混淆。由于这种限制使模型无法模拟真实状况，因此需要写出更复杂、更有弹性、含未知参数的函数，并引出如何构造这样的函数这一问题。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that linear models have significant limitations, and this limitation arising from the model itself is called model bias. It clarifies that this model bias differs from the parameter b, which is also called bias, and notes the terminology is ambiguous. Because this limitation prevents the model from simulating real situations, a more complex, more flexible function with unknown parameters is needed, and the unit ends by raising the question of how to write such a function.

points.title: 线性模型的限制称为 Model Bias
Model Bias 与参数 b（Bias）用词上的区别
需要更复杂、有弹性的含未知参数函数

chapters.title: 用常数项与蓝色函数叠加逼近红色折线
chapters.summary: 说明红色折线可视为一个常数项加上多个蓝色函数之和。蓝色函数在阈值前为定值，中间有斜坡，之后又为定值。常数项取红色折线与x轴交点大小，各蓝色函数的斜坡起点与终点分别对齐红色折线的转折点，并令斜率一致，依次相加即可得到红色折线的各段。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that the red piecewise-linear curve can be viewed as a constant term plus a sum of blue functions. Each blue function is constant before one threshold, has a sloped middle segment, and is constant after another threshold. The constant is set to the red curve's x-axis intercept, and each blue function's slope start and end are aligned with successive turning points of the red curve, with matching slopes, so adding them cumulatively reproduces each segment of the red curve.

points.title: 蓝色函数的形状：水平、斜坡、水平
常数项取红色曲线与x轴交点
第一个蓝色函数对齐第一个转折点
第二个蓝色函数对齐第一到第二个转折点
第三个蓝色函数生成第二个转折点之后的部分

chapters.title: 分段线性曲线可由常数项与多个蓝色函数组合而成
chapters.summary: 说明分段线性曲线由多段锯齿状线段组成，可用常数项加上多个蓝色函数组合出来；曲线转折点越多，需要的蓝色函数就越多。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that piecewise linear curves are made of many jagged line segments and can be formed by a constant term plus multiple blue functions; the more turning points the curve has, the more blue functions are needed.

points.title: 分段线性曲线的定义：由多段线段组成
用常数项加多个蓝色函数组合出分段线性曲线
转折点越多，所需蓝色函数越多

chapters.title: 用分段线性曲线逼近任意连续曲线
chapters.summary: 说明即使 x 与 y 的关系不是分段线性曲线，也可以通过在曲线上取足够多且位置适当的点并连成折线，使其逼近原来的连续曲线；而每个分段线性曲线又可由多个蓝色函数相加表示，因此只要蓝色函数足够多，就能表示任意连续曲线，进而用带未知数的函数来拟合复杂关系。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that even if the relationship between x and y is not piecewise linear, one can sample enough appropriately placed points on the curve and connect them into a piecewise linear curve that approximates the original continuous curve; since each piecewise linear curve can be composed from many blue functions, enough blue functions can approximate any continuous curve, so a function with unknowns can represent a complex relationship.

points.title: 在非分段线性曲线上取点并连成折线
取点足够多或位置适当时折线可逼近连续曲线
分段线性曲线可由多个蓝色函数组合而成
足够多的蓝色函数相加可逼近任意连续曲线
用带未知数的函数表示复杂关系

chapters.title: 用 Sigmoid 函数逼近蓝色函数
chapters.summary: 本段说明如何用 Sigmoid 函数来逼近一个难以直接写出式子的蓝色函数。Sigmoid 的输入 x1 先乘 w 加 b，取负后取指数再加 1 作为分母，前面可乘常数 c。当 x1 趋近正无穷时输出收敛到 c，趋近负无穷时输出趋近 0。Sigmoid 意为 S 型函数，之后简写为 y = c·Sigmoid(b + w·x1)。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how to approximate a blue function whose formula is hard to write directly by using a Sigmoid function. The Sigmoid takes input x1, multiplies it by w, adds b, negates the result, exponentiates it, adds 1, and places that in the denominator, with an optional constant c in front. As x1 approaches positive infinity the output converges to c, and as x1 approaches negative infinity the output approaches 0. The name Sigmoid means S-shaped, and the expression is later abbreviated as y = c·Sigmoid(b + w·x1).

points.title: 用 Sigmoid 函数逼近蓝色函数
Sigmoid 函数的式子结构
x1 趋近正无穷时输出收敛到 c
x1 趋近负无穷时输出趋近 0
Sigmoid 名称含义与简写形式

chapters.title: 用 Sigmoid 逼近 Hard Sigmoid 函數
chapters.summary: 說明可用 Sigmoid Function 逼近圖中的藍色函數，而該藍色函數常見名稱是 Hard Sigmoid；並解釋因教學順序先介紹藍色函數再介紹 Sigmoid，才先以 Sigmoid 逼近的角度切入。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that a Sigmoid function can approximate the blue function shown, and that this blue function is commonly called a Hard Sigmoid; also notes the teaching order of introducing the blue function before the Sigmoid.

points.title: Sigmoid 可逼近藍色函數
藍色函數常稱為 Hard Sigmoid
因教學順序而先以逼近角度說明

chapters.title: 调整 Sigmoid 函数的参数以逼近目标曲线
chapters.summary: 说明如何通过调整 b、w、c 三个参数制造不同形状的 Sigmoid 函数：改 w 改变斜率与坡度，改 b 使函数左右移动，改 c 改变高度；将不同 Sigmoid 叠加后可逼近各种分段线性函数，进而近似各种连续函数。
chapters.english_summary: Explains how adjusting the parameters b, w, and c produces Sigmoid functions of different shapes: changing w alters the slope/steepness, changing b shifts the function left or right, and changing c changes its height. Stacking different Sigmoid functions allows approximating various piecewise linear functions, which in turn can approximate various continuous functions.

points.title: 需要各种合适的蓝色 Function 来组成曲线
调整 b、w、c 制造不同形状的 Sigmoid
改 w 改变斜率与坡度
改 b 使 Sigmoid 左右移动
改 c 改变高度，叠加后逼近分段线性与连续函数

chapters.title: 红色折线函数的组成与蓝色函数参数表示
chapters.summary: 说明红色折线可视为0加三个蓝色函数之和，每个蓝色函数形式为对x1乘w加b做Sigmoid再乘c，并分别用w1b1c1、w2b2c2、w3b3c3表示三个蓝色函数的参数。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that the red piecewise line can be written as 0 plus the sum of three blue functions, each of the form sigmoid(x1*w+b)*c, with the three blue functions using parameters w1 b1 c1, w2 b2 c2, and w3 b3 c3 respectively.

points.title: 红色折线等于0加三个蓝色函数之和
蓝色函数的固定形式：sigmoid(x1*w+b)*c
三个蓝色函数分别使用w1b1c1、w2b2c2、w3b3c3

chapters.title: 用 Sigmoid 加總建構彈性函式以降低模型偏誤
chapters.summary: 說明將常數項與多個帶有未知參數的 Sigmoid 函式相加，可得到一個有彈性的函式；透過調整不同的 c、b、w 參數，能組合出不同的 piecewise linear 曲線，進而逼近各種連續函式，以減少線性模型的偏誤。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that summing a constant with multiple sigmoid terms containing unknown parameters yields a flexible function; by varying c, b, and w, one can produce different piecewise linear curves to approximate various continuous functions and reduce the bias of a linear model.

points.title: 將常數與多個 Sigmoid 項相加得到函式形式
Summation 代表把不同藍色函式加總
b、w、c 為未知參數，可調整以產生不同藍色函式
疊加不同紅色曲線可形成 piecewise linear 曲線並逼近連續函式
以彈性函式取代線性模型以減少模型偏誤

chapters.title: 多特征输入与弹性函数扩展
chapters.summary: 说明用编号 j 表示多个特征，举例前28天对应 j=1到28、前56天对应 j=1到56；并把原本的 b+Σwjxj 扩展为 Sigmoid 内 bi+Σwijxj，每个 Sigmoid 有不同 bi 与 wij，取 Sigmoid 后乘 ci 全部相加再加 b 得到 y，改变 ci、bi、wij 即可得到不同函数。
chapters.english_summary: Explains using index j for multiple features, with examples of j from 1 to 28 for the previous 28 days and 1 to 56 for the previous 56 days, and extends the function by replacing the term inside Sigmoid with bi plus a weighted sum over j, where each Sigmoid has its own bi and wij, then multiplying each Sigmoid output by ci, summing them, and adding b to get y; changing ci, bi, and wij yields different functions.

points.title: 用 j 表示特征编号及天数范围示例
把函数扩展为 Sigmoid 内 bi+Σwijxj
每个 Sigmoid 有不同 bi 与 wij，输出乘 ci 相加再加 b
改变 ci、bi、wij 可得到不同函数

chapters.title: 用图示直观理解多个Sigmoid函数的加权求和
chapters.summary: 当公式仍显抽象时，用图示方式展示其实际运算。以j=1,2,3为例，只考虑前一天、前两天、前三天三个特征x1、x2、x3，每个i代表一个用Sigmoid近似的蓝色函数，共三个Sigmoid。第一个Sigmoid将x1乘w11、x2乘w12、x3乘w13后相加再加b；第二个Sigmoid对应w21、w22、w23加b2；第三个Sigmoid对应w31、w32、w33加b3。wij表示第i个Sigmoid中乘给第j个特征的权重。
chapters.english_summary: This unit gives an intuitive diagrammatic explanation of the weighted sums inside multiple sigmoid functions. Using j=1,2,3 with features x1, x2, x3 representing view counts from the previous one, two, and three days, each i denotes one sigmoid approximating a blue function. It shows that the first sigmoid computes x1*w11 + x2*w12 + x3*w13 + b, the second uses w21, w22, w23 plus b2, and the third uses w31, w32, w33 plus b3, with wij denoting the weight applied to the j-th feature in the i-th sigmoid.

points.title: 以j=1,2,3三个特征为例进行图示
每个i代表一个Sigmoid函数
第一个Sigmoid括号内的加权求和
wij下标含义：第i个Sigmoid中第j个特征的权重
第二、第三个Sigmoid括号内的运算

chapters.title: 用矩陣與向量簡化神經網路運算
chapters.summary: 將三個 Sigmoid 括弧內的加權和分別記為 r1、r2、r3，並說明可把 x1、x2、x3 組成向量 x，把九個權重組成矩陣 W，把 b1、b2、b3 組成向量 b，將原本三個式子簡寫成 x 乘上 W 再加上 b 得到向量 r。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how to simplify the three weighted-sum expressions inside the sigmoid functions by naming them r1, r2, and r3, then rewriting the computation in linear algebra notation: stack x1, x2, x3 into a vector x, arrange the nine weights into a matrix W, stack b1, b2, b3 into a vector b, and express the result as x multiplied by W plus b to obtain vector r.

points.title: 將三個括弧內結果命名為 r1、r2、r3
說明 r 與輸入特徵 x 的加權和關係
將 x、權重、b、r 分別組成向量與矩陣
簡寫成 x 乘上 W 再加上 b 得到 r
強調兩種表示方式運算完全相同

chapters.title: 从线性组合到Sigmoid激活：由x得到a的过程
chapters.summary: 本段讲解蓝色虚线框内的计算流程：先将输入x乘以权重w并加上偏置b，得到r1、r2、r3；再让每个r分别通过Sigmoid函数，即对r取负号后做指数运算再加1，取倒数得到a1、a2、a3，最终完成从x1、x2、x3到a1、a2、a3的转换。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the computation inside the blue dashed box: first multiply input x by weight w and add bias b to obtain r1, r2, r3; then pass each r through the Sigmoid function, taking the negative of r, exponentiating it, adding 1, and using the reciprocal to get a1, a2, a3, thereby transforming x1, x2, x3 into a1, a2, a3.

points.title: 线性组合：x乘w加b得到r1、r2、r3
r1、r2、r3分别通过Sigmoid函数
Sigmoid计算细节：取负、指数、加1、取倒数
由r1、r2、r3得到a1、a2、a3
蓝色虚线框内完成从x1x2x3到a1a2a3的转换

chapters.title: 用 Sigmoid 函數的簡潔符號表示向量運算
chapters.summary: 說明如何用一個簡潔符號表示向量 r 通過 Sigmoid 函數的運算，將 r1、r2、r3 分別通過 Sigmoid 後得到 a1、a2、a3，並以該符號直接代表整個運算。
chapters.english_summary: Explains a concise notation for applying the Sigmoid function to a vector r, where r1, r2, and r3 are each passed through the Sigmoid function to produce a1, a2, and a3, using a single symbol to represent this operation.

points.title: 引入簡潔表示法：用符號代表通過 Sigmoid 函數
將 r1、r2、r3 分別通過 Sigmoid 得到 a1、a2、a3

chapters.title: 用向量與矩陣表示 Sigmoid 輸出加權求和
chapters.summary: 說明將 Sigmoid 輸出 a1、a2、a3 分別乘上 c1、c2、c3 後相加再加上 b 得到 y，並改寫成向量形式：向量 a 乘上向量 c 的轉置再加上 b。接著把整串運算整理為 x 乘上矩陣 w 加向量 b 得到 r，經 Sigmoid 得到 a，再乘上 c 的轉置加 b 得到 y，指出圖示化與線性代數兩種表示方式其實在講同一件事。
chapters.english_summary: Explains how the Sigmoid outputs a1, a2, a3 are multiplied by c1, c2, c3, summed, and added to b to produce y, then rewritten in vector form as vector a times the transpose of vector c plus b. It then consolidates the whole computation as x times matrix w plus vector b giving r, passing r through a Sigmoid to get a, and multiplying a by the transpose of c plus b to get y, noting that the diagrammatic and linear-algebra representations describe the same thing.

points.title: Sigmoid 輸出乘上 c 再加 b 得到 y
改寫為向量形式：a 乘 c 的轉置加 b
整串運算的線性代數表示：xW+b 經 Sigmoid 再乘 c 轉置加 b
圖示化與線性代數兩種表示方式其實相同

chapters.title: 重新定義符號：將未知參數統一表示為 θ
chapters.summary: 講者重新定義符號，說明 x 是 Feature，w、b、c 等為未知參數，並將這些參數拉直拼成一個長向量，統稱為 θ，以改寫機器學習的第一步。
chapters.english_summary: The instructor redefines notation: x is the feature, while w, b, and c are unknown parameters. These parameters are flattened and concatenated into a long vector denoted as θ, which collectively represents all unknown parameters, rewriting the first step of machine learning.

points.title: x 是 Feature，w、b、c 是未知參數
將 w、b、c 拉直拼成長向量 θ
θ 統稱所有未知參數

chapters.title: 课堂问答：优化方法、Sigmoid 数量与 Hard Sigmoid
chapters.summary: 本段为课堂问答环节。教师回应了三个问题：一是为何不能暴力搜索所有参数，而需用梯度下降；二是 Sigmoid 的数量可自行决定，数量越多可产生越复杂的分段线性函数，但属于超参数；三是也可以直接使用 Hard Sigmoid，不一定只能用 Sigmoid 逼近，并预告后续会讲其他做法。
chapters.english_summary: This is a Q&A segment. The instructor answers three questions: why brute-force search over all parameters is not feasible and gradient descent is needed; that the number of sigmoids is a hyperparameter chosen by the user, and more sigmoids allow more complex piecewise linear functions; and that Hard Sigmoid can be used directly, not only approximated by sigmoid, with other approaches to be covered later.

points.title: 为何需要梯度下降而非暴力搜索参数
Sigmoid 数量是超参数，越多可产生越复杂的分段线性函数
也可以直接使用 Hard Sigmoid，不一定只能用 Sigmoid 逼近

chapters.title: 第二步：定義損失函數（以 θ 統稱所有參數）
chapters.summary: 說明進入第二步定義 Loss。新的模型雖然參數變多，但 Loss 的定義方式與只有兩個參數時相同，只是改用 θ 統稱所有未知參數，Loss Function 寫成 L(θ)，用來評估某一組 θ 數值的好壞。計算是先給定一組 θ（即各 w、b、c 等參數值），代入 feature x 得到估測的 y，再與真實 label 比較得到誤差 e，最後把所有誤差加總即為 Loss。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the second step of defining the loss. With the new model, the loss is defined the same way as before, but all unknown parameters are collectively denoted by θ, so the loss function becomes L(θ), which evaluates how good or bad a given set of θ values is. The computation is unchanged: assign a set of θ values (the various w, b, c parameters), plug in a feature x to get the predicted y, compare it with the true label to obtain an error e, and sum all errors to get the loss.

points.title: 進入第二步：定義 Loss
用 θ 統稱所有未知參數，Loss 改寫為 L(θ)
Loss 的計算方式與只有兩個參數時相同
代入一組 θ 與 feature x，得到估測 y 並與真實 label 比較
把所有誤差加總得到 Loss

chapters.title: 优化步骤与梯度下降：从参数向量到梯度更新
chapters.summary: 说明优化问题与之前相同，仍使用梯度下降；参数θ是长向量，目标是找到使Loss最小的θ*。先随机初始化θ⁰，对每个参数计算对L的微分并集合成梯度向量g（用∇L(θ⁰)表示），再用θ⁰减去learning rate乘g得到θ¹，如此反复更新直到停止或梯度为零向量。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that the optimization problem is unchanged and still uses gradient descent. The parameter theta is a long vector, and the goal is to find the theta that minimizes the loss. It describes randomly initializing theta^0, computing the derivative of the loss for each parameter and collecting them into a gradient vector g, denoted with a nabla symbol, then updating parameters by subtracting the learning rate times the gradient to get theta^1, and repeating until stopping or the gradient becomes a zero vector.

points.title: 优化问题与梯度下降不变
随机初始化θ⁰并计算梯度g
梯度记号∇L(θ⁰)的含义
用θ⁰减learning rate乘g更新参数
反复更新直到停止或梯度为零向量

chapters.title: 實作細節：Batch、Update 與 Epoch 的區別
chapters.summary: 說明梯度下降實作時會將大 N 筆資料隨機分成多個 Batch，每次只用一個 Batch 的資料計算 Loss（如 L1、L2、L3）與 Gradient 來更新參數；並定義看過所有 Batch 為一個 Epoch、每次更新參數為一次 Update，最後用兩個例子計算一個 Epoch 內的更新次數，並指出 Batch Size 是 HyperParameter。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains the practical detail of gradient descent: splitting N data points into randomly formed batches of size B, computing a loss (L1, L2, L3) and gradient from one batch at a time to update parameters, defining an epoch as seeing all batches once and an update as one parameter update, and using two examples to compute how many updates occur in one epoch, noting batch size is a hyperparameter.

points.title: 將資料隨機分成 Batch，每次用一個 Batch 算 Loss 與 Gradient
Update 與 Epoch 的定義不同
例子：10000 筆資料、Batch Size 10，一個 Epoch 更新 1000 次
例子：1000 筆資料、Batch Size 100，一個 Epoch 更新 10 次
Batch Size 是 HyperParameter

chapters.title: 用 ReLU 取代 Sigmoid：Hard Sigmoid 的替代做法
chapters.summary: 說明 Hard Sigmoid 不一定要換成 Soft Sigmoid，可用兩個 ReLU（Rectified Linear Unit）相加來表示，並介紹 ReLU 的式子 c·max(0, b+wx1) 與其圖形。若要達到原本 i 個 Sigmoid 的效果，需使用約 2 倍的 ReLU。最後指出 Sigmoid 與 ReLU 統稱為 Activation Function，並提到後續實驗選擇 ReLU。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that a Hard Sigmoid need not be replaced by a soft Sigmoid, since it can be formed by summing two Rectified Linear Units (ReLUs). Describes the ReLU form c·max(0, b+wx1) and its shape, notes that matching i Sigmoids may require about twice as many ReLUs, and states that Sigmoid and ReLU are collectively called activation functions, with ReLU chosen in later experiments.

points.title: Hard Sigmoid 可由兩個 ReLU 相加而成
ReLU 的式子與圖形：c·max(0, b+wx1)
用 ReLU 取代 Sigmoid 時需要約 2 倍數量
Sigmoid 與 ReLU 統稱為 Activation Function
後續實驗選擇 ReLU，原因留待下週說明

chapters.title: 不同數量 ReLU 的實驗結果比較
chapters.summary: 以真實數據比較線性模型與不同數量 ReLU 的表現：56 天訓練下，線性模型訓練 Loss 為 0.32k、2021 年未見資料為 0.46k；10 個 ReLU 與線性差不多，100 個 ReLU 使訓練 Loss 降至 0.28k 並在測試資料上略有改善，1000 個 ReLU 訓練 Loss 更低但未見資料上進步不大。
chapters.english_summary: The speaker reports real experimental results comparing a linear model with models using different numbers of ReLU units over 56 days: the linear model has training loss 0.32k and 2021 unseen-data loss 0.46k; 10 ReLUs show little improvement, 100 ReLUs lower training loss to 0.28k and slightly improve test performance, and 1000 ReLUs lower training loss further but show little improvement on unseen data.

points.title: 線性模型與 10 個 ReLU 的基準結果
100 個 ReLU 的訓練與測試表現
1000 個 ReLU 的訓練與未見資料表現

chapters.title: 反覆堆疊運算以擴充模型
chapters.summary: 說明可以將 x 乘上 w 加 b 再通過激活函數得到 a 的運算反覆多做幾次，例如把 a 再乘上另一組 w' 加 b' 並通過 Sigmoid 或 ReLU 得到 a'，並指出重複次數是需自行決定的超參數，且各層的 w、b 並非同一組參數。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that the operation of multiplying x by w, adding b, and passing through an activation function to get a can be repeated several times, for example multiplying a by another w' plus b' and passing through Sigmoid or ReLU to get a'; the number of repetitions is a hyperparameter to decide, and the w and b at each step are not the same parameters.

points.title: 原本從 x 到 a 的運算：乘 w 加 b 再過激活函數
激活函數不限定 Sigmoid，ReLU 也可以
把同樣運算反覆多做幾次：a 再經 w'、b' 與激活函數得到 a'
重複次數是需自行決定的超參數
各層的 w、b 不是同一組參數，會增加更多未知參數

chapters.title: 增加ReLU层数的实验结果
chapters.summary: 本段展示增加ReLU层数的实验结果：每次加100个ReLU，输入为56天前的数据。一层时Loss为0.28k，两层降到0.18k，三层降到0.14k；在未见过的数据上从0.43k降到0.38k，显示层数增加带来进步。
chapters.english_summary: This unit presents experimental results of stacking ReLU layers, adding 100 ReLUs each time with input features from 56 days prior. It reports training loss dropping from 0.28k with one layer to 0.18k with two layers and 0.14k with three layers, and unseen-data loss decreasing from 0.43k to 0.38k, indicating improvement.

points.title: 实验设置：每次加100个ReLU，输入为56天前数据
一层（乘w加b过一次ReLU）的Loss为0.28k
两层时Loss降到0.18k
三层时Loss降到0.14k
未见过的数据上Loss从0.43k降到0.38k

chapters.title: 三次 ReLU 模型的真实实验结果与除夕低谷分析
chapters.summary: 展示使用三次 ReLU 的模型预测结果，横轴为日期，纵轴为观看人次（千人），红线为真实数据，蓝线为预测数据。模型能准确预测周期性低点，但在除夕当天出现明显低谷时，模型晚一天才预测出低谷，因为模型只看前 56 天的值，不知道除夕是什么。
chapters.english_summary: This unit presents real experimental results from a model using three ReLU layers. The horizontal axis is date and the vertical axis is viewership in thousands. The red line is real data and the blue line is predicted data. The model accurately predicts periodic low points, but on Lunar New Year's Eve, when there is a clear dip, the model predicts the dip one day late because it only looks at the previous 56 days and does not know what Lunar New Year's Eve is.

points.title: 实验设置与坐标轴说明
模型准确预测周期性低点
除夕低谷预测延迟现象
原因：模型不知道除夕

chapters.title: 從 Neuron 到 Neural Network 再到 Deep Learning 的命名故事
chapters.summary: 本段說明 Sigmoid 或 ReLU 等單元稱為 Neuron，多個 Neuron 組成 Neural Network，並以人腦神經元作類比。接著提到 Neural Network 一詞在 80、90 年代已被使用且因過度吹捧而名聲不佳，因此後來以 Layer、Hidden Layer、Deep 等新名稱重新包裝，整套技術便稱為 Deep Learning。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that Sigmoid or ReLU units are called neurons, and many neurons form a neural network, compared to neurons in the human brain. It notes that the term neural network was already used in the 1980s and 1990s and had a bad reputation due to overhype, so new names such as layer, hidden layer, and deep were used to rebrand the technology as deep learning.

points.title: Sigmoid 或 ReLU 單元稱為 Neuron
多個 Neuron 組成 Neural Network，並類比人腦神經元
Neural Network 在 80、90 年代已使用且因過度吹捧而名聲不佳
以 Layer、Hidden Layer、Deep 等新名稱重新包裝
整套技術稱為 Deep Learning

chapters.title: 类神经网络层数演进与影像辨识错误率
chapters.summary: 讲述类神经网络越叠越深的发展趋势，列举 AlexNet、VGG、GoogleNet、Residual Net 的层数与影像辨识错误率，并指出训练深层网络需要诀窍。
chapters.english_summary: Explains the trend of stacking neural networks deeper, listing AlexNet, VGG, GoogleNet, and Residual Net with their layer counts and image recognition error rates, and notes that training very deep networks requires special techniques.

points.title: AlexNet：8层，错误率16.4%
VGG：19层，错误率7.3%
GoogleNet：22层，错误率6.7%
Residual Net：152层
训练深层网络需要诀窍

chapters.title: 深度学习的深层意义：为何不把网络变胖？
chapters.summary: 本段提出一个关于深度网络必要性的疑问：既然足够多的 ReLU 或 Sigmoid 排成一排就能逼近任何连续函数，那么反复使用这些激活函数（即把网络变深）的意义何在？有人因此认为深度学习只是噱头，因为“Deep”听起来比“Fat”更厉害。讲者指出这是日后要再讲的话题。
chapters.english_summary: This unit raises a question about the rationale for deep networks: if enough ReLU or Sigmoid units arranged in a single layer can approximate any continuous function, what is the benefit of repeatedly applying them (making the network deep)? It mentions a skeptical view that deep learning is just a gimmick because 'Deep' sounds more impressive than 'Fat' neural networks, and states this will be discussed later.

points.title: 回顾：足够多的 ReLU/Sigmoid 可逼近任何连续函数
提出疑问：反复使用激活函数（变深）的意义何在？
有人质疑深度学习只是噱头，因为“Deep”名字好听
对比 Fat Neural Network 与 Deep Neural Network 的命名
指出这是日后要再讲的话题

chapters.title: 加深网络层数导致的过拟合现象
chapters.summary: 本段讨论将网络从3层加深到4层后的效果。4层在训练资料上Loss为0.1k，优于3层；但在未看过的2021年资料上Loss为0.44k，反而比3层差。训练资料与未见资料结果不一致，这种状况称为Overfitting（过拟合）。
chapters.english_summary: This unit discusses what happens when the network is made deeper, going from 3 layers to 4 layers. The 4-layer model achieves a loss of 0.1k on training data, better than 3 layers, but on unseen 2021 data its loss is 0.44k, worse than 3 layers. The inconsistency between results on training data and unseen data is called Overfitting.

points.title: 提出加深网络到4层的动机
4层在训练资料与未见资料上的Loss对比
训练资料与未见资料结果不一致
这种状况称为Overfitting

chapters.title: 模型選擇：預測未見資料時應選三層網路
chapters.summary: 講者指出，雖然已有 2021 年 2 月 14 日前的資料並訓練出模型，但尚未真正發揮模型力量。真正目標是預測未知資料，例如 2 月 26 日的觀看人數。他讓學生舉手表決該選三層還是四層網路，多數人選三層。他解釋，四層網路在訓練資料上表現較好，但我們在意的是沒看過的資料，因此應選擇在未見資料上表現好的模型，也就是三層網路。
chapters.english_summary: The instructor explains that although a model has been trained on data up to February 14, 2021, the real goal is to predict unseen data, such as viewership on February 26. He polls students on whether to choose a 3-layer or 4-layer network, with most choosing 3 layers. He notes that while a 4-layer network performs better on training data, what matters is performance on unseen data, so the 3-layer network should be selected.

points.title: 尚未發揮模型力量，真正目標是預測未知資料
舉例：預測 2 月 26 日未知觀看人數，該選三層還是四層網路
課堂表決：多數學生選擇三層網路
關鍵理由：不在意訓練資料結果，而在意未見過的資料表現
結論：應選擇三層網路

chapters.title: 用三層網路預測 YouTube 觀看次數的課堂尾聲
chapters.summary: 講者延續課程，實際用三層網路模型預測頻道 2 月 26 日的觀看次數。因 YouTube 統計只到 2 月 24 日，先假設模型對 2 月 25 日的預測 5250 人正確，再預測 2 月 26 日為 3960 次，並解釋模型因週五觀看較少而預測偏低。講者比較此預測與 0.38k 的誤差，詢問學生看法，預告下週驗證，最後開玩笑說講這麼久是騙大家去點影片。
chapters.english_summary: The instructor continues the lesson by using a three-layer network model to predict the channel's YouTube views for February 26. Since YouTube analytics only go up to February 24, the model first predicts 5,250 views for February 25; assuming that is correct, it then predicts 3,960 views for February 26. The instructor explains the lower prediction is because the model knows Fridays have fewer viewers, compares this prediction's error with 0.38k, asks students to raise hands on whether the error will be smaller or larger, and says they will check next week. The instructor jokes that the long talk was just to trick everyone into clicking the video.

points.title: 模型預測 2 月 25 日觀看人次為 5250 人
模型預測 2 月 26 日觀看次數為 3960 次
解釋預測偏低是因為模型知道週五觀看人數較少
比較預測誤差與 0.38k 並詢問學生看法
預告下週驗證實際值並開玩笑說騙大家點影片

chapters.title: 课程总结与延伸资源
chapters.summary: 讲师总结本次深度学习课程，说明本讲采用非一般介绍方式，并提示若想听一般介绍可参考过去课程影片链接；同时提到深度学习训练使用的 Backpropagation 是较有效率的梯度计算方法，与本讲内容本质相同，并附上相关影片链接。最后宣布下课并致谢。

The instructor also mentions that Backpropagation, used in deep learning training, is an efficient way to compute gradients and is not fundamentally different from today's material, providing a video link for it. The lecture ends with thanks.

chapters.title: 太空中的毁灭性威胁
chapters.summary: 本单元介绍太空中多种可能毁灭地球生命的威胁，包括小行星、伽马射线暴和超新星，并引出一种似乎比这些更可怕、能摧毁所到之处一切的事物。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces various threats in outer space that could destroy life on Earth, including asteroids, gamma-ray bursts, and supernovae, and teases something in space that seems more terrifying than any of these and wipes out everything it comes near.

points.title: 小行星可毁灭整个物种
伽马射线暴和超新星可能灭绝地球生命
太空中不乏能肆虐地球的力量
引出比这些更可怕的事物
该事物能摧毁所到之处的一切

chapters.title: 地球会被黑洞吞噬吗？——黑洞与事件视界简介
chapters.summary: 本单元以“地球会被黑洞吞噬吗？”这一问题开场，解释黑洞是密度极大的天体，会不可逃脱地改变周围时空，使其弯曲成无限深的陷阱；任何东西包括光，一旦越过事件视界，都无法以足够快的速度逃离黑洞引力。黑洞被比喻为容量无限的宇宙吸尘器，会吞掉路径上的一切，什么也不放出来。
chapters.english_summary: This unit opens with the question of whether Earth could be swallowed by a black hole. It explains that a black hole is an extremely dense object that inescapably modifies and warps space and time around it into an infinite sink. Nothing, not even light, can move fast enough to escape its gravitational pull once it passes the event horizon. The black hole is described as a cosmic vacuum cleaner with infinite capacity that gobbles up everything in its path and lets nothing out.

points.title: 开场问题：地球会被黑洞吞噬吗？
黑洞密度极大，会不可逃脱地改变周围时空
连光也无法逃离黑洞引力，事件视界是边界
黑洞被比喻为容量无限的宇宙吸尘器

chapters.title: 如何定位不发光的黑洞
chapters.summary: 本段解释黑洞不发光，但可通过其对周围空间的影响来观测：物质靠近时被巨大引力加速并发出强光；太远而未被吸入的物体轨道仍受引力影响；若观察到多颗恒星绕看似空无一物的点运行，可能是黑洞在主导；光线靠近事件视界会被偏折，即引力透镜效应。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how black holes can be located despite not emitting light, by observing their effects on surrounding space: matter approaching a black hole is accelerated by its immense gravitational field and emits enormous light; objects too far to be pulled in still have their orbits affected by the gravitational force; several stars orbiting an apparently empty point could indicate a black hole; and light passing close to an event horizon is deflected via gravitational lensing.

points.title: 黑洞不发光，但可通过周围空间效应观测
物质靠近黑洞被加速并发出强光
远处物体轨道仍受黑洞引力影响
多颗恒星绕空点运行可能暗示黑洞
光线靠近事件视界被偏折：引力透镜

chapters.title: 恒星级黑洞：形成与数量
chapters.summary: 介绍较小的一类黑洞——恒星级黑洞，其质量可达太阳的100倍，由大质量恒星耗尽核燃料后核心坍缩形成；已观测到距离约3000光年的此类天体，银河系中可能多达1亿个。
chapters.english_summary: Explains stellar mass black holes: their mass can be up to 100 times the sun's, they form when a massive star uses up its nuclear fuel and its core collapses, several have been observed as close as 3000 light-years away, and there could be up to 100 million in the Milky Way.

points.title: 恒星级黑洞的质量上限
由大质量恒星核心坍缩形成
已观测到约3000光年外的实例
银河系中可能多达1亿个

chapters.title: 恒星黑洞是否值得担忧
chapters.summary: 本段讨论恒星黑洞是否构成威胁。虽然其质量巨大，但半径仅约300公里或更小，直接撞击地球的概率极小。不过其引力场可远距离影响行星，若典型恒星质量黑洞经过海王星附近，地球轨道会被显著改变并带来严重后果。但考虑到黑洞体积小、星系广阔，恒星黑洞并不太值得担忧。
chapters.english_summary: This unit addresses whether stellar black holes are a threat. Despite their large mass, they have a radius of around 300 kilometers or less, making a direct hit with Earth minuscule. However, their gravitational fields can affect a planet from a large distance, so they could be dangerous without a direct collision; if a typical stellar-mass black hole passed near Neptune, Earth's orbit would be considerably modified with dire results. Still, because they are small and the galaxy is vast, stellar black holes are not much to worry about.

points.title: 直接撞击概率极小
引力场可远距离影响行星
经过海王星附近会改变地球轨道
体积小与星系广阔使威胁有限

chapters.title: 超大质量黑洞：特征与位置
chapters.summary: 本单元介绍第二类黑洞——超大质量黑洞。它们的质量是太阳的数百万到数十亿倍，事件视界可跨越数十亿公里。它们通过吞噬物质和与其他黑洞合并而增长。与恒星级黑洞不同，它们不游荡，而是位于星系中心，包括银河系中心。我们的太阳系以安全距离绕银河系中心的超大质量黑洞稳定运行。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces the second type of black hole: supermassive black holes. It explains that they have masses millions or billions of times greater than the sun and event horizons spanning billions of kilometers. They grow by swallowing matter and merging with other black holes. Unlike stellar black holes, they are not wandering but lie at the centers of galaxies, including the Milky Way. The solar system orbits the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center at a safe distance of 25,000 light-years.

points.title: 超大质量黑洞的质量与事件视界
超大质量黑洞的增长方式
超大质量黑洞位于星系中心
太阳系绕银河系中心黑洞运行

chapters.title: 银河系碰撞可能将地球推向黑洞
chapters.summary: 本段说明地球目前安全的状态可能改变：若银河系与其他星系碰撞，地球可能被抛向银河系中心，靠近超大质量黑洞并最终被吞噬。文中提到预计40亿年后会与仙女座星系发生碰撞，这对地球可能不是好消息。
chapters.english_summary: The transcript explains that Earth's current situation could change if the galaxy collides with another, potentially throwing Earth toward the galactic center close enough to the supermassive black hole to be swallowed. It states that a collision with the Andromeda Galaxy is predicted in 4 billion years, which may not be good news for Earth.

points.title: 碰撞可能改变地球轨道
地球可能被抛向银河系中心并被黑洞吞噬
预计40亿年后与仙女座星系碰撞

chapters.title: 黑洞并非毁灭者：塑造星系与宇宙的功臣
chapters.summary: 本段指出不应片面地将黑洞视为毁灭力量，强调黑洞在星系形成中发挥了关键作用，星系是宇宙的组成部分；黑洞并非宇宙舞台上的阴暗角色，而是从根本上让宇宙变得明亮而惊人的重要贡献者。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that black holes should not be judged only as destructive agents; it states they played a crucial role in the formation of galaxies, the building blocks of the universe, and fundamentally contributed to making the universe a bright and astonishing place.

points.title: 不应过于苛刻地评判黑洞
黑洞在星系形成中的关键作用
黑洞让宇宙变得明亮而惊人

videos.title: 【機器學習2021】類神經網路訓練不起來怎麼辦 (二)： 批次 (batch) 與動量 (momentum)
videos.creator: Hung-yi Lee

chapters.title: Batch 與 Momentum 訓練技巧：Batch 的運作方式
chapters.summary: 本單元介紹訓練時使用 Batch 的原因與做法：將所有資料分成一個個 Batch（或 Mini Batch），每次用一個 Batch 的資料計算 Loss 與 Gradient 並更新參數，而非用全部資料一起計算；所有 Batch 看過一遍稱為一個 Epoch；並說明 Shuffle 是在每個 Epoch 開始前重新分 Batch，使每個 Epoch 的 Batch 組成不同。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces why and how Batch is used in training: data is split into batches (also called mini batches), and each parameter update uses one batch to compute loss and gradient rather than all data at once; seeing all batches once is called an epoch; Shuffle means re-splitting batches before each epoch so batch composition differs each epoch.

points.title: 為什麼訓練時要用 Batch
Batch 的運作：用一個 Batch 算 Loss、Gradient 並更新參數
Epoch 的定義：所有 Batch 看過一遍
Shuffle：每個 Epoch 開始前重新分 Batch

chapters.title: 為什麼要使用 Batch：Full Batch 與 Batch Size 等於 1 的比較
chapters.summary: 以 20 筆訓練資料為例，比較兩種極端情況：不使用 Batch（Full Batch）時需看完所有資料才能計算 Loss 與 Gradient 並更新一次參數；Batch Size 等於 1 時每看一筆資料就更新一次參數，一個 Epoch 可更新 20 次。說明前者更新方向較穩定但更新次數少，後者更新頻繁但方向較 Noisy、曲折，並指出兩者各有優缺點，且平行運算會影響對更新時間的判斷。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains why batch is used by comparing two extreme cases with 20 training examples: full batch (no batch), where all examples must be seen before computing loss and gradient and updating parameters once, versus batch size 1, where parameters are updated after each single example, giving 20 updates per epoch. It describes the full-batch update as more stable but less frequent, and the batch-size-1 update as noisier and more zigzagging, notes each has advantages and disadvantages, and mentions that parallel computation affects whether the full-batch approach necessarily takes longer.

points.title: 以 20 筆訓練資料比較 Full Batch 與 Batch Size 等於 1
Full Batch：看完所有資料才計算 Loss、Gradient 並更新一次參數
Batch Size 等於 1：每看一筆資料就更新一次參數，一個 Epoch 更新 20 次
Batch Size 等於 1 的 Loss 較 Noisy，更新方向曲曲折折
兩者各有優缺點，且平行運算會影響對更新時間的判斷

chapters.title: 批次大小與訓練時間的實驗結果
chapters.summary: 本單元透過 MNIST 手寫數字辨識實驗，說明較大 Batch Size 計算 Loss 與 Gradient 的時間不一定比小 Batch Size 長，因為 GPU 平行運算使 Batch Size 從 1 到 1000 的耗時幾乎相同；但 Batch Size 極大時時間仍會增長。同時比較 Update 一次參數與跑完一個 Epoch 的時間，指出大 Batch Size 反而讓一個 Epoch 更快完成。
chapters.english_summary: This unit presents experimental results on batch size and training time using MNIST handwritten digit classification. It explains that with GPU parallel computation, computing loss and gradient for batch sizes from 1 to 1000 takes nearly the same time, though very large batch sizes increase time. It also contrasts time per parameter update versus time per epoch, showing that larger batch sizes can make an epoch faster.

points.title: MNIST 手寫數字辨識實驗設定
GPU 平行運算使小到中等 Batch Size 耗時相近
極大 Batch Size 時 GPU 計算時間仍會增長
Update 一次參數與跑完一個 Epoch 的時間趨勢相反
大 Batch Size 反而讓一個 Epoch 更快完成

chapters.title: 大 Batch 在 GPU 平行運算下的時間優勢
chapters.summary: 說明若使用 GPU，大 Batch 與小 Batch 每次 Update 的運算時間可能相同，因此大 Batch 在技能冷卻時間上並不較吃虧，甚至佔有優勢，其原本的劣勢似乎消失。
chapters.english_summary: Explains that with GPU parallel computation, updating on a large batch may take about the same time as updating on a small batch, so the large batch's skill cooldown time is not longer and its disadvantage seems to disappear, leaving mainly advantages.

points.title: 用技能冷卻時間描述 Batch Size 差異並不精確
GPU 下大 Batch 與小 Batch 的 Update 時間可能相同
大 Batch 的劣勢消失後似乎只剩優勢

chapters.title: 小批量训练中噪声梯度为何有助于优化
chapters.summary: 本段解释小批量（Small Batch）训练中噪声梯度反而有助于训练的反直觉现象。通过 MNIST 和 CIFAR-10 实验说明：批量越大，训练集和验证集上的正确率都越差，这不是过拟合，而是优化问题。可能的原因是：全批量（Full Batch）更新时若遇到梯度为零的局部最小值或鞍点就会卡住；而小批量每次使用不同批次的损失函数（L1、L2 等），即使 L1 卡住，L2 的梯度不一定为零，因此仍能继续更新参数、降低损失。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains why noisy gradients from small batch training can help optimization. It uses MNIST and CIFAR-10 results to show that larger batch sizes lead to worse training and validation accuracy, indicating an optimization issue rather than overfitting. A possible explanation is that full-batch updates can get stuck at local minima or saddle points where the gradient is zero, while small batches use different loss functions (L1, L2, etc.) per update, so if one batch's gradient is zero, another batch may still provide a nonzero gradient and allow training to continue.

points.title: MNIST 与 CIFAR-10 上批量大小对正确率的影响
大批量导致训练和验证结果都变差，不是过拟合
同一模型下大批量带来优化问题
全批量更新可能卡在梯度为零的局部最小值或鞍点
小批量使用不同损失函数，噪声更新帮助继续训练

chapters.title: 小批量训练对测试表现的帮助
chapters.summary: 本段介绍一个反直觉现象：即使通过调整学习率等方法让大批量与小批量在训练集上达到相近的准确率，小批量在测试集上仍表现更好。引用论文《On Large-Batch Training For Deep Learning: Generalization Gap And Sharp Minima》的实验，在CNN和全连接网络等不同设置下验证该现象。小批量每批256笔，大批量每批6000笔（数据集60000笔的0.1倍）。训练准确率相近时，测试时小批量反而更好，说明大批量可能过拟合。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that even when large-batch and small-batch training are tuned to achieve similar training accuracy, small batches can still perform better at testing. It cites experiments from the paper 'On Large-Batch Training For Deep Learning: Generalization Gap And Sharp Minima' across CNNs and fully connected networks, with small batch size 256 and large batch size 6000 (0.1 of a 60000-example dataset). The observed testing gap suggests overfitting for large batches.

points.title: 小批量对测试也有帮助
引用论文实验设置
大小批量训练到相近准确率
测试时小批量更好，暗示过拟合

chapters.title: 大/小批次與損失曲面：好壞極小值的解釋
chapters.summary: 本段解釋為何大、小批次可能導致不同泛化表現：假設訓練與測試損失函數存在差異（分佈不同或取樣不同），可視為訓練損失向右平移。位於狹窄峽谷的極小值在平移後損失劇增，屬於壞極小值；位於寬廣盆地的極小值則變化小，屬於好極小值。直覺上，小批次因更新方向隨機，容易跳出窄峽谷而停在寬盆地；大批次則較可能走入窄峽谷。此解釋並非人人接受，仍是待研究問題。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains a proposed reason why large and small batch sizes may lead to different generalization. It describes training loss with multiple local minima, distinguishing bad minima in narrow valleys from good minima in broad basins. Assuming a mismatch between training and testing loss (due to different distributions or sampling), the training loss is shifted, causing valley minima to have much worse testing loss while basin minima change little. It then presents the intuition that small batches, with noisy updates, tend to escape narrow valleys and settle in wide basins, whereas large batches follow updates more directly and may end up in narrow valleys. The explanation is noted as not universally accepted and still an open research question.

points.title: 好壞極小值的定義：峽谷 vs. 盆地
訓練與測試損失不匹配：損失函數平移的假設
平移對峽谷與盆地極小值的影響
小批次因更新隨機性易跳出窄峽谷
大批次傾向走入窄峽谷；此解釋仍待研究

chapters.title: 大小 Batch 的比較與 Batch Size 作為超參數
chapters.summary: 比較小 Batch 與大 Batch 在運算時間、每個 Epoch 所需時間、更新方向穩定性及最佳化與測試表現上的差異，並指出 Batch Size 是需要調整的超參數。
chapters.english_summary: Compares small and large batch sizes in terms of computation time, time per epoch, noisiness of update direction, and optimization and testing performance, concluding that batch size is a hyperparameter that needs to be tuned.

points.title: 有無平行運算下的大小 Batch 運算時間
每個 Epoch 所需時間：大 Batch 較快
更新方向：小 Batch 較 Noisy、大 Batch 較穩定
Noisy 更新在 Optimization 與 Testing 的優勢
Batch Size 是需要調整的超參數

chapters.title: 大 Batch 與小 Batch 的優點能否兼得
chapters.summary: 本單元討論能否同時取得大 Batch 與小 Batch 的優點：用大 Batch Size 與平行運算提升訓練效率，同時得到好的訓練結果。講者指出這是可能的，並提及相關論文，例如 76 分鐘訓練 BERT、15 分鐘訓練 ResNet、一分鐘訓練 ImageNet，這些快速訓練是因為 Batch Size 開得很大，例如第一篇論文使用三萬筆 Example 的 Batch Size。最後提到需要特別方法來解決大 Batch Size 可能帶來的劣勢。
chapters.english_summary: This unit discusses whether it is possible to combine the advantages of large and small batch sizes: using a large batch size and parallel computation to improve training efficiency while still achieving good training results. The speaker says this is possible and mentions related papers, such as training BERT in 76 minutes, ResNet in 15 minutes, and ImageNet in one minute, attributing the speed to very large batch sizes, for example a batch size of 30,000 examples in the first paper. It ends by noting that special methods are needed to address the potential disadvantages of large batch sizes.

points.title: 能否兼得大 Batch 與小 Batch 的優點
用大 Batch Size 與平行運算提升訓練效率
相關論文舉例：快速訓練 BERT、ResNet、ImageNet
大 Batch Size 的實例：三萬筆 Example
需要特別方法解決大 Batch Size 的劣勢

chapters.title: 动量法（Momentum）概念引入：用物理惯性对抗鞍点与局部极小值
chapters.summary: 本段介绍动量法（Momentum）这一技术，说明它可能用于对抗鞍点（Saddle Point）或局部极小值（Local Minima）。讲者用物理类比解释其概念：把误差曲面（Error Surface）想象成真实斜坡，参数是一个球；梯度下降走到局部极小值或鞍点就停住，而物理世界中的球因惯性从高处滚下时，即使到鞍点或局部极小值，只要动量够大仍会继续向右滚动，甚至翻过小坡。由此引出能否把这一概念用到梯度下降中，即接下来要讲的动量法。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces Momentum as another technique that may help overcome Saddle Points or Local Minima. It explains the concept through a physics analogy: treating the Error Surface as a real slope and the parameters as a ball rolling downhill. Gradient Descent stops at a Local Minima or Saddle Point, but a physical ball with inertia keeps moving right past a Saddle Point, and if its momentum is large enough, it can continue past a Local Minima and even roll over a small hill. The speaker then asks whether this concept can be applied to Gradient Descent, setting up the upcoming discussion of Momentum.

points.title: 动量法可能对抗鞍点或局部极小值
物理类比：误差曲面如斜坡，参数如滚动的球
梯度下降会停在局部极小值或鞍点
球因惯性可越过鞍点，动量够大还能翻过小坡
引出将惯性概念用于梯度下降的动量法

chapters.title: 梯度下降法快速複習
chapters.summary: 本單元快速複習一般的梯度下降法（Vanilla Gradient Descent）的運作流程：從初始參數 θ0 開始，計算梯度後往梯度反方向更新參數，到達新參數後再計算梯度、再更新，如此反覆進行。
chapters.english_summary: This unit quickly reviews the vanilla gradient descent procedure: starting from an initial parameter θ0, computing the gradient, updating the parameter in the opposite direction of the gradient, then recomputing the gradient at the new parameter and updating again, repeating this process.

points.title: Vanilla Gradient Descent 的定義與名稱由來
從初始參數 θ0 開始計算梯度
往梯度反方向更新參數
反覆計算梯度並更新參數的流程

chapters.title: 动量梯度下降：结合梯度与上一步更新方向
chapters.summary: 本单元讲解在梯度下降中加入动量（Momentum）后的参数更新方式：每次移动参数时，不仅考虑梯度的反方向，还加上前一步的更新方向，两者相加决定新的更新方向。以初始参数为例，前一步更新量设为0，因此第一步与普通梯度下降相同；从第二步起，更新方向变为前一次更新方向与当前梯度反方向的组合。配合图示说明梯度指示方向与前一步方向相加后取折中方向移动，并反复进行该过程，强调与普通梯度下降不同，会同时考虑之前移动的方向。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how adding Momentum changes gradient descent: instead of moving parameters only opposite to the gradient, each update combines the negative gradient direction with the previous update direction. It walks through initialization where the previous update is set to zero, so the first step matches ordinary gradient descent, then from the second step onward the update direction is based on the previous update direction and the current gradient. A diagram is used to show adding the gradient-indicated direction and the previous-step direction to move in a compromise direction, repeating this process, and contrasting it with ordinary gradient descent by considering prior movement direction.

points.title: 加入动量后更新方向为梯度反方向加上前一步移动方向
初始化时前一步更新量设为0，第一步与普通梯度下降相同
从第二步开始更新方向由前一次更新方向与当前梯度组合决定
用图示说明梯度方向与前一步方向相加后取折中方向移动
反复进行同样操作，与普通梯度下降不同，会考虑之前移动方向

chapters.title: 动量法中移动量的梯度加权和解释
chapters.summary: 本段解释动量法中每一步移动量 m 可写成过去所有梯度的加权和。通过递推式 m0=0、m1=m0-ηg0、m2=λm1-ηg1 等，说明 m2 是 g0 与 g1 的加权和，并指出 λ 是需调节的参数。由此得出动量法的另一种解读：更新方向不只考虑当前梯度，而是考虑过去所有梯度的总和。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that in momentum, each movement m can be written as a weighted sum of all past gradients. Using the recurrence m0=0, m1=m0-ηg0, m2=λm1-ηg1, it shows m2 is a weighted sum of g0 and g1, notes λ is a tunable parameter, and concludes that momentum updates consider the sum of all past gradients rather than only the current gradient.

points.title: 移动量 m 可表示为过去梯度的加权和
递推式推导：m1 与 m2 的表达式
λ 是另一个需要调节的参数
m2 是 g0 与 g1 的加权和
动量法的另一种解读：考虑过去所有梯度的总和

chapters.title: 动量法直观示例讲解
chapters.summary: 通过一个简单例子说明动量（Momentum）如何更新参数：结合梯度方向与前一步移动方向，使参数在梯度变小、为零（局部极小值或鞍点）甚至梯度反向时仍能继续前进，可能越过小丘到达更好的局部极小值。
chapters.english_summary: A simple worked example explaining how Momentum updates parameters by combining the gradient direction with the previous step's direction, so movement can continue even when the gradient is small, zero at a local minimum or saddle point, or points the opposite way, potentially crossing a small hill to reach a better local minimum.

points.title: 第一步按梯度方向更新参数
梯度变小但叠加前一步方向继续右移
在局部极小值或鞍点仍可凭前一步方向前进
前一步影响大于梯度时可能反向越过小丘
动量可能带来的好处与内容收尾

videos.title: The beneficial bacteria that make delicious food - Erez Garty
videos.creator: TED-Ed

chapters.title: 食物发酵现象引入
chapters.summary: 本单元通过面包蓬松、瑞士奶酪孔洞和醋的酸味三个例子，引出这些现象都源于微小生物消耗糖分并产生烹饪副产物的过程。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces three food phenomena—bread's fluffiness, Swiss cheese's holes, and vinegar's sourness—and states that they all come from tiny organisms consuming sugar and producing culinary byproducts.

points.title: 面包为何蓬松
瑞士奶酪为何有孔洞
醋为何酸
共同来源：微生物消耗糖分并产生副产物

chapters.title: 酵母的发酵与有氧代谢：面包松软结构的形成
chapters.summary: 介绍酵母作为单细胞真菌在面包、啤酒和葡萄酒制作中的作用，说明其分解碳水化合物获取能量的两种途径：有氧途径和厌氧发酵。重点解释面包烘焙中酵母通常先进行厌氧发酵，产生乙醇和二氧化碳，乙醇在烘焙时蒸发；有氧途径则消耗糖并产生二氧化碳和水。两种过程产生的二氧化碳被面筋捕获形成气泡，赋予面包海绵状结构和柔软质地。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces yeast as single-celled fungi used in bread, beer, and wine. It explains that yeast break down carbohydrates like sugar for energy via two pathways: the oxygen-dependent aerobic pathway and the oxygen-independent anaerobic pathway, also called fermentation. In bread baking, yeast can use both but normally start with anaerobic fermentation, producing ethanol and CO2; the small amount of alcohol evaporates during baking. In the aerobic pathway, yeast consume sugar and produce CO2 and water. In both processes, CO2 accumulates as tiny bubbles trapped by gluten, creating a sponge-like structure that gives bread its soft texture.

points.title: 酵母的定义与用途
酵母分解碳水化合物的两种途径
面包烘焙中酵母的厌氧发酵及乙醇蒸发
有氧途径产生二氧化碳和水
二氧化碳气泡被面筋捕获形成海绵结构

chapters.title: 葡萄酒酿造中的酵母发酵与二氧化碳处理
chapters.summary: 本段讲解葡萄酒酿造依赖酵母，在低氧条件下酵母通过无氧发酵消耗糖分。过程常始于葡萄上的野生酵母，但为获得稳定结果，多数酿酒师会添加能耐受高酒精度的精选酵母。糖分下降时酒精上升；更甜的酒不一定酒精度更低，因为不同葡萄含糖量不同，也可额外加糖。二氧化碳则通过排气口逸出；在香槟、啤酒等碳酸酒精饮料中，会使用密封容器在初次或二次发酵中保留二氧化碳。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that wine-making relies on yeast and keeps oxygen levels low so yeast ferment sugar anaerobically. It notes that the process often starts with wild yeasts on grapes, but most winemakers add selected yeast strains that tolerate high alcohol for consistency. As sugar drops, alcohol rises; sweeter wines do not necessarily have less alcohol because grape sugar levels vary and sugar can be added. Carbon dioxide bubbles away through a vent, while carbonated alcoholic beverages like champagne and beer use sealed containers during primary or secondary fermentation to keep carbon dioxide in the bottle.

points.title: 低氧条件下酵母通过无氧发酵消耗糖分
野生酵母与添加耐高酒精精选酵母
糖分下降与酒精上升，甜度与酒精度无必然关系
二氧化碳通过排气口逸出
密封容器在初次或二次发酵中保留二氧化碳

chapters.title: 葡萄酒中的细菌：从风味到醋
chapters.summary: 本单元介绍葡萄酒中的细菌。一种特殊菌株能将葡萄汁中的酸味化合物转化为更柔和的风味物质，赋予红葡萄酒和霞多丽部分风味；而醋酸菌在有氧气时会将乙醇转化为醋酸，持续作用则得到醋。
chapters.english_summary: This unit introduces bacteria in wine. A special strain converts tart compounds in grape juice into softer-tasting ones responsible for some flavors in red wines and chardonnays. Acetic acid bacteria, when oxygen is present, convert ethanol into acetic acid, and if the process continues, vinegar results.

points.title: 特殊菌株将酸味化合物转化为柔和风味
醋酸菌将乙醇转化为醋酸
持续作用最终得到醋

chapters.title: 细菌如何制作奶酪：发酵、凝乳与不同菌种的作用
chapters.summary: 本段讲解细菌在奶酪制作中的关键作用：牛奶接种细菌后，细菌消耗乳糖产生乳酸等化学物质，使牛奶酸度升高，蛋白质聚集凝结；通常还会加入哺乳动物体内的凝乳酶促进该过程，凝乳最终被压榨成硬质奶酪。不同菌种产生不同奶酪，例如产二氧化碳的菌种赋予瑞士奶酪孔洞，布里和卡门贝尔奶酪还使用霉菌。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains how bacteria are key to making cheese: milk is inoculated with bacteria, which consume lactose and produce lactic acid and other chemicals; as acidity rises, milk proteins aggregate and curdle. Cheesemakers usually add rennet, an enzyme naturally found in cows, goats, and some other mammals, to help the process. Curds are pressed to remove water and form firm cheese. Different bacterial strains make different cheeses, such as a carbon-dioxide-emitting species giving Swiss cheese its holes, and brie and camembert also using mold.

points.title: 细菌消耗乳糖产生乳酸，使牛奶酸化并凝结
通常加入凝乳酶促进凝结过程
凝乳被压榨去水形成硬质奶酪
不同菌种制作不同奶酪，如瑞士奶酪的孔洞
布里和卡门贝尔奶酪还使用霉菌

chapters.title: 厨房：微生物的生物技术实验室
chapters.summary: 本单元将厨房比作由微生物运作的生物技术实验室，并列举了酸奶、酱油、酸奶油、酸菜、开菲尔、泡菜、康普茶、切达奶酪、哈拉面包、皮塔饼和馕等发酵食品，最后以一句玩笑提醒这些未必适合出现在同一顿晚餐中。
chapters.english_summary: This unit describes the kitchen as a biotechnology lab run by microorganisms that culture cuisine, lists fermented foods such as yogurt, soy sauce, sour cream, sauerkraut, kefir, kimchi, kombucha, cheddar, challah, pita, and naan, and ends with a joke that they may not all belong at the same dinner.

points.title: 厨房被比作由微生物运作的生物技术实验室
列举多种发酵食品
玩笑：这些未必适合同一顿晚餐

chapters.title: 凌晨备考与演奏会：睡眠可能比临时抱佛脚更有效
chapters.summary: 视频以凌晨4点、8小时后有重要考试和钢琴演奏会的场景开场，提出在尚未准备好的情况下，与其继续喝咖啡、临时抱佛脚和练习，不如合上书、收起乐谱去睡觉。
chapters.english_summary: The video opens with a scenario at 4 a.m. before a big test in eight hours and a piano recital, asking what one can do. It contrasts drinking more coffee and cramming or practicing with the possibility that closing the books, putting away the music, and going to sleep might be better.

已学习并练习多日但仍未准备好
选择继续喝咖啡、临时抱佛脚和练习
可能更好的选择是合上书、收起乐谱去睡觉

chapters.title: 睡眠并非浪费时间：被忽视的关键生理功能
chapters.summary: 本段指出睡眠占据人生近三分之一，却常被忽视，根源在于一种重大误解：睡眠不是失去的时间或完成重要工作后的休息，而是一项关键功能，期间身体平衡并调节呼吸、循环、生长和免疫反应等生命系统。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that sleep occupies nearly a third of life but is often neglected due to a major misunderstanding: sleep is not lost time or merely rest after important work, but a critical function during which the body balances and regulates vital systems, affecting respiration and regulating everything from circulation to growth and immune response.

points.title: 睡眠占据人生近三分之一却常被忽视
忽视睡眠源于一种重大误解
睡眠不是失去的时间或事后的休息
睡眠是调节呼吸、循环、生长和免疫的关键功能

chapters.title: 睡眠对大脑的重要性
chapters.summary: 本段说明睡眠对大脑至关重要：入睡时身体约五分之一的循环血液被输送到大脑，而睡眠期间大脑处于高度活跃的重组阶段，这对记忆的运作至关重要。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that sleep is crucial for the brain: about a fifth of the body's circulatory blood is channeled to the brain as one drifts off, and the brain during sleep undergoes an intensely active period of restructuring that is crucial for how memory works.

points.title: 入睡时约五分之一循环血液流向大脑
睡眠中大脑处于高度活跃的重组阶段
这一重组过程对记忆运作至关重要

chapters.title: 记忆的遗忘曲线与巩固：海马体的作用
chapters.summary: 本单元介绍记忆的局限性：19世纪心理学家赫尔曼·艾宾浩斯证明，我们通常会在20分钟内忘记40%的新材料，即遗忘曲线。这种遗忘可通过记忆巩固来防止，即信息从短暂的短期记忆转移到更持久的长时记忆的过程。巩固需要大脑的海马体。20世纪50年代，布伦达·米尔纳对患者H.M.的研究表明，海马体被切除后，H.M.形成新短期记忆和长时记忆的能力受损，但仍能通过重复学习身体任务。该案例揭示海马体专门参与长时陈述性记忆（如事实和概念）的巩固，而非程序性记忆（如手指动作）。
chapters.english_summary: This unit explains that memory is limited: 19th-century psychologist Herman Ebbinghaus demonstrated the forgetting curve, showing we normally forget 40% of new material within twenty minutes. This loss can be prevented through memory consolidation, the process of moving information from fleeting short-term memory to durable long-term memory, which occurs with the help of the hippocampus. It describes 1950s research by Brenda Milner with patient H.M., whose hippocampus was removed; his ability to form new short-term memories was damaged, but he could learn physical tasks through repetition, and his long-term memory formation was also damaged. The case revealed the hippocampus is specifically involved in consolidating long-term declarative memory, such as facts and concepts for a test, rather than procedural memory, such as finger movements for a recital.

points.title: 艾宾浩斯的遗忘曲线：20分钟内遗忘40%新内容
记忆巩固：信息从短期记忆转入长时记忆
海马体在长时记忆形成中的作用
布伦达·米尔纳与H.M.案例：海马体切除的影响
海马体专门参与陈述性记忆而非程序性记忆的巩固

chapters.title: 记忆巩固的当前模型：从短时记忆到长时记忆
chapters.summary: 本段介绍米尔纳与埃里克·坎德尔的研究所确立的记忆巩固模型：感觉数据先被转录并暂时记录为短时记忆，随后传至海马体，海马体强化该皮层区域的神经元；借助神经可塑性，形成新的突触芽，建立神经元间的新连接并强化神经网络，信息最终返回成为长时记忆。
chapters.english_summary: This unit describes the current model of memory consolidation based on Milner's findings and Eric Kandel's 1990s work: sensory data is first transcribed and temporarily recorded as short-term memory, then travels to the hippocampus, which strengthens neurons in the cortical area; through neuroplasticity, new synaptic buds form, creating new connections between neurons and strengthening the neural network, after which the information returns as long-term memory.

points.title: 感觉数据先被转录为短时记忆
信息传至海马体并强化皮层神经元
神经可塑性形成新突触芽与新连接
信息返回成为长时记忆

chapters.title: 记忆为何因人而异：情绪与睡眠的作用
chapters.summary: 本单元提出为何有些事会被记住、有些不会，并指出影响记忆保持程度与效果的若干因素。举例说明：在情绪高涨甚至压力状态下形成的记忆，会因海马体与情绪的联系而被更好地记录；而促进记忆巩固的主要因素之一是良好的夜间睡眠。
chapters.english_summary: This unit asks why some things are remembered and others are not, then notes that several factors influence the extent and effectiveness of memory retention. It gives the example that memories formed during heightened feeling or even stress are better recorded because of the hippocampus's link with emotion, and states that one major factor contributing to memory consolidation is a good night's sleep.

points.title: 影响记忆保持程度与效果的因素
情绪高涨或压力下形成的记忆因海马体与情绪的联系而被更好记录
良好夜间睡眠是记忆巩固的主要因素之一

chapters.title: 睡眠阶段与记忆巩固：慢波睡眠和REM睡眠的不同作用
chapters.summary: 睡眠由四个阶段组成，最深的是慢波睡眠和快速眼动睡眠。脑电图监测显示，脑干、海马体、丘脑和皮层之间存在电脉冲，这些区域是记忆形成的接力站。不同睡眠阶段有助于巩固不同类型的记忆：非快速眼动的慢波睡眠中，陈述性记忆被编码到海马体前部的临时存储中，并通过皮层与海马体的持续对话反复激活，逐渐重新分布到皮层的长期存储中；而快速眼动睡眠则与程序性记忆的巩固有关。
chapters.english_summary: Sleep consists of four stages, with the deepest being slow-wave sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. EEG monitoring shows electrical impulses moving between the brainstem, hippocampus, thalamus, and cortex, which act as relay stations for memory formation. Different sleep stages help consolidate different types of memories: during non-REM slow-wave sleep, declarative memory is encoded into a temporary store in the anterior hippocampus and, through ongoing dialogue between the cortex and hippocampus, is repeatedly reactivated and gradually redistributed to long-term storage in the cortex. REM sleep, resembling waking brain activity, is associated with the consolidation of procedural memory.

points.title: 睡眠的四个阶段及最深阶段
脑区间的电脉冲与记忆形成接力站
不同睡眠阶段巩固不同类型记忆
慢波睡眠中陈述性记忆的编码与再激活
REM睡眠与程序性记忆巩固

chapters.title: 基于研究的最佳睡眠时间安排
chapters.summary: 本片段根据研究结论指出，在记忆公式后三小时入睡、练习音阶后一小时入睡是最理想的安排。
chapters.english_summary: This unit states that, based on studies, the most ideal timing is to go to sleep three hours after memorizing formulas and one hour after practicing scales.

points.title: 记忆公式后三小时入睡
练习音阶后一小时入睡

chapters.title: 睡眠不足损害长期健康与记忆巩固
chapters.summary: 本段总结睡眠不足不仅损害长期健康，还会降低前一晚所学知识与练习的保留效果，印证了“睡一觉再想”的智慧。睡眠期间大脑进行内部重组和建立新连接，因此充足睡眠能让人每天醒来拥有更新、更完善的大脑，迎接挑战。
chapters.english_summary: This closing unit states that skimping on sleep harms long-term health and makes it less likely that knowledge and practice from the previous night will be retained, affirming the phrase 'Sleep on it.' It explains that during sleep the brain undergoes internal restructuring and forms new connections, so proper sleep leads to waking up with a new and improved brain ready for challenges.

points.title: 睡眠不足损害长期健康并降低知识保留
睡眠期间大脑内部重组与建立新连接
充足睡眠带来更新更完善的大脑

chapter.title: 睡眠阶段与记忆巩固：慢波睡眠和REM睡眠的不同作用
chapter.summary: 睡眠由四个阶段组成，最深的是慢波睡眠和快速眼动睡眠。脑电图监测显示，脑干、海马体、丘脑和皮层之间存在电脉冲，这些区域是记忆形成的接力站。不同睡眠阶段有助于巩固不同类型的记忆：非快速眼动的慢波睡眠中，陈述性记忆被编码到海马体前部的临时存储中，并通过皮层与海马体的持续对话反复激活，逐渐重新分布到皮层的长期存储中；而快速眼动睡眠则与程序性记忆的巩固有关。
chapter.english_summary: Sleep consists of four stages, with the deepest being slow-wave sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. EEG monitoring shows electrical impulses moving between the brainstem, hippocampus, thalamus, and cortex, which act as relay stations for memory formation. Different sleep stages help consolidate different types of memories: during non-REM slow-wave sleep, declarative memory is encoded into a temporary store in the anterior hippocampus and, through ongoing dialogue between the cortex and hippocampus, is repeatedly reactivated and gradually redistributed to long-term storage in the cortex. REM sleep, resembling waking brain activity, is associated with the consolidation of procedural memory.

chapter.title: 睡眠阶段与记忆巩固：慢波睡眠和REM睡眠的不同作用
chapter.summary: 睡眠由四个阶段组成，最深的是慢波睡眠和快速眼动睡眠。脑电图监测显示，脑干、海马体、丘脑和皮层之间存在电脉冲，这些区域是记忆形成的接力站。不同睡眠阶段有助于巩固不同类型的记忆：非快速眼动的慢波睡眠中，陈述性记忆被编码到海马体前部的临时存储中，并通过皮层与海马体的持续对话反复激活，逐渐重新分布到皮层的长期存储中；而快速眼动睡眠则与程序性记忆的巩固有关。
chapter.english_summary: Sleep consists of four stages, with the deepest being slow-wave sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. EEG monitoring shows electrical impulses moving between the brainstem, hippocampus, thalamus, and cortex, which act as relay stations for memory formation. Different sleep stages help consolidate different types of memories: during non-REM slow-wave sleep, declarative memory is encoded into a temporary store in the anterior hippocampus and, through ongoing dialogue between the cortex and hippocampus, is repeatedly reactivated and gradually redistributed to long-term storage in the cortex. REM sleep, resembling waking brain activity, is associated with the consolidation of procedural memory.

results.creator: Google Cloud Tech
results.reason: 该片段直接讲解 MCP 的客户端-服务器架构：服务器如何暴露资源与工具、客户端如何动态发现能力，以及通过结构化 JSON 请求/响应进行通信，完整覆盖连接工具与数据的基本机制。

chapter.title: MCP 工作原理：客户端与服务器
chapter.summary: 解释 MCP 的核心架构：协议分为客户端和服务器两侧。客户端通常是语言模型或代理系统，服务器是暴露资源的环境。服务器连接后会声明其支持的能力、资源和操作，使模型无需预先编程即可动态发现 API。双方通过简单明确定义的 schema 通信，客户端发送请求，服务器返回结构化 JSON。
chapter.english_summary: Explains the core architecture of MCP: the protocol has two sides, clients and servers. The client is usually the language model or agent system, while the server is the environment exposing resources. Upon connection, the server advertises its supported capabilities, resources, and actions, allowing the model to dynamically discover APIs without pre-programming. Communication uses a simple, well-defined schema where the client sends requests and the server responds with structured JSON.

chapter.title: MCP 协议的核心资源类型：工具、资源、提示与上下文
chapter.summary: 本段深入讲解 MCP 协议定义的几类主要资源类型：工具是模型可调用的动作（如搜索数据库、发邮件、分析文件）；资源是数据与状态（如文本文档、数据库记录、图像）；提示是描述模型在特定任务中行为的可复用模板；上下文是模型可引入推理过程的外部信息（如聊天历史、公司数据、用户偏好）。MCP 客户端连接后可向服务器请求这些内容的列表，每个工具或资源都带有描述其功能、输入与输出的元数据，使模型能智能交互。协议在所有工具间强制统一 schema，因此无论使用 GitHub、CRM 还是日历服务器，模型都使用同一种语言。
chapter.english_summary: This unit explains the main MCP resource types: tools as invokable actions (e.g., search database, send email, analyze a file), resources as data and state (e.g., text document, database record, image), prompts as reusable templates for model behavior on specific tasks, and context as external information pulled into reasoning (e.g., chat history, company data, user preferences). It also covers how an MCP client can request lists of these from the server, how each tool or resource carries metadata about its function, expected input, and returned output, and how the protocol enforces a consistent schema so models speak the same language across GitHub, CRM, or calendar servers.

chapter.title: MCP 实践示例：个人助理代理的集成对比
chapter.summary: 通过构建个人助理代理的示例，对比传统 API 集成方式与 MCP 方式。传统方式需为 Google Calendar、Notion、Gmail 分别编写代码、处理认证和边缘情况，并用冗长脆弱的系统提示教模型使用端点；MCP 方式则安装各系统服务器，服务器声明能力，模型自动发现工具并推理使用顺序和数据传递，开发者无需编写胶水代码，因为协议一致。
chapter.english_summary: A practical example compares building a personal assistant agent with traditional API integrations versus MCP. In the old approach, developers integrate Google Calendar, Notion, and Gmail APIs, write code for each service, handle authentication, rate limits, and edge cases, and teach the model via long fragile system prompts. With MCP, developers build or install servers for each system (calendar, note, email), each advertising capabilities; the model automatically sees available tools like list events, get meeting summary, or send email, and reasons about what to use, in what order, and what data to pass. The key difference is no glue code per new tool because the protocol is consistent.

chapter.title: 小批量训练中噪声梯度为何有助于优化
chapter.summary: 本段解释小批量（Small Batch）训练中噪声梯度反而有助于训练的反直觉现象。通过 MNIST 和 CIFAR-10 实验说明：批量越大，训练集和验证集上的正确率都越差，这不是过拟合，而是优化问题。可能的原因是：全批量（Full Batch）更新时若遇到梯度为零的局部最小值或鞍点就会卡住；而小批量每次使用不同批次的损失函数（L1、L2 等），即使 L1 卡住，L2 的梯度不一定为零，因此仍能继续更新参数、降低损失。
chapter.english_summary: This unit explains why noisy gradients from small batch training can help optimization. It uses MNIST and CIFAR-10 results to show that larger batch sizes lead to worse training and validation accuracy, indicating an optimization issue rather than overfitting. A possible explanation is that full-batch updates can get stuck at local minima or saddle points where the gradient is zero, while small batches use different loss functions (L1, L2, etc.) per update, so if one batch's gradient is zero, another batch may still provide a nonzero gradient and allow training to continue.

chapter.title: 酵母的发酵与有氧代谢：面包松软结构的形成
chapter.summary: 介绍酵母作为单细胞真菌在面包、啤酒和葡萄酒制作中的作用，说明其分解碳水化合物获取能量的两种途径：有氧途径和厌氧发酵。重点解释面包烘焙中酵母通常先进行厌氧发酵，产生乙醇和二氧化碳，乙醇在烘焙时蒸发；有氧途径则消耗糖并产生二氧化碳和水。两种过程产生的二氧化碳被面筋捕获形成气泡，赋予面包海绵状结构和柔软质地。
chapter.english_summary: This unit introduces yeast as single-celled fungi used in bread, beer, and wine. It explains that yeast break down carbohydrates like sugar for energy via two pathways: the oxygen-dependent aerobic pathway and the oxygen-independent anaerobic pathway, also called fermentation. In bread baking, yeast can use both but normally start with anaerobic fermentation, producing ethanol and CO2; the small amount of alcohol evaporates during baking. In the aerobic pathway, yeast consume sugar and produce CO2 and water. In both processes, CO2 accumulates as tiny bubbles trapped by gluten, creating a sponge-like structure that gives bread its soft texture.
